question: Who won India's first Olympic medals at the 1900 Paris Games by securing silver in 200m sprint and 200m hurdles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Norman Pritchard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Norman Pritchard was the first athlete from India to win an Olympic medal at the **1900 Paris Games**.
 
• He won two **silver medals** in athletics: one in the **200m sprint** and the other in the **200m hurdles**.
 
• Pritchard is recognized as the **first Asian-born athlete** to win an Olympic medal.
 
• He competed under the British Indian flag since India was under British rule during that time.
 
• Norman Pritchard was also a **professional actor** in Hollywood, where he was known as Norman Trevor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milkha Singh**

 
 
• Milkha Singh, also known as the "Flying Sikh," was one of India's greatest athletes and a legendary sprinter.
 
• He represented India in the Olympics in 1956, 1960, and 1964, with his most notable performance being at the **1960 Rome Olympics**, where he narrowly missed a bronze medal in the 400m race.
 
• Milkha Singh won gold medals in the **1958 and 1962 Asian Games** and the 1958 Commonwealth Games.
 
 
 
• **K.D. Jadhav**
 
 
• Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav was an Indian wrestler who won a bronze medal in the **1952 Helsinki Olympics**.
 
• He was the first Indian athlete to win an individual Olympic medal in independent India.
 
• Jadhav competed in the **Bantamweight category** of freestyle wrestling and is remembered for his incredible agility and technique.
 
 
 
• **Dhyan Chand**
 
 
• Dhyan Chand, also known as "The Wizard of Hockey," was one of the greatest hockey players in history.
 
• He was a key player in the Indian hockey team that won gold medals in the **1928, 1932, and 1936 Olympics**.
 
• Dhyan Chand is known for his exceptional ball control, goal-scoring ability, and contribution to India's dominance in hockey during his era.
